People are the strategy.

WorkAtlas Consult Limited provides human resources, workforce and organisational advisory services to help organisations build stronger people practices and navigate change with clarity.

Privacy notice.

How WorkAtlas Consult Limited may collect, use and protect information when you visit this website or contact us.

OverviewInformation we collectHow we use dataCookiesSharing & retentionYour choicesContact us
This privacy notice explains how WorkAtlas Consult Limited handles personal information. It should be reviewed periodically to ensure it reflects current practices and applicable data protection requirements.

1. Overview

WorkAtlas Consult Limited (“WorkAtlas”, “we”, “us” or “our”) respects privacy and aims to handle personal information responsibly. This notice explains how information may be collected and used when you browse this website, submit an enquiry or otherwise interact with us through the website.

2. Information we collect

Depending on how you use the website, we may collect information you choose to provide, such as your name, business email address, telephone number, organisation, service enquiry and the contents of your message. Basic technical information may also be processed to operate, secure and understand website performance, subject to your cookie choices and applicable requirements.

Please do not submit confidential employee files, health information or other sensitive personal information through the general contact form unless WorkAtlas has provided a suitable secure channel and instructions.

3. How we use information

  • Respond to enquiries and requests for consultation.
  • Communicate about services you have asked us about.
  • Maintain website security, functionality and performance.
  • Meet applicable legal obligations and protect our legitimate interests where permitted.
  • Use optional analytics or marketing technologies only in accordance with the choices presented and applicable law.

4. Cookies and similar technologies

Cookies are small files stored on your device. Essential cookies may be used for security, navigation and remembering your privacy preferences. Optional analytics or marketing cookies should remain disabled unless you choose to enable them. You can revisit your preferences at any time using “Cookie settings” in the website footer.

5. Sharing, security and retention

We do not sell personal information. Information may be handled by authorised service providers who support website hosting, communications, security or analytics, subject to appropriate safeguards. We aim to retain information only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose collected, legal obligations or resolving disputes. No website or transmission method can be guaranteed completely secure.

6. Your choices and rights

Depending on applicable law, you may have rights to request access to, correction or deletion of personal information, object to or restrict certain processing, or withdraw consent where processing relies on consent. You may also change optional cookie preferences through this website. We may need to verify your identity before responding.

7. Contact us

For privacy questions or requests, contact WorkAtlas Consult Limited at ibukun@workatlasconsult.com or visit 3a, Chief Collins Street, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos, Nigeria.

    WorkAtlas Insights · HR Management

    Building a strong HR foundation as your business grows

    As an organisation grows, informal people processes can become difficult to manage. A clear HR foundation helps teams make consistent decisions, communicate expectations and support employees through the employment lifecycle.

    Start with clear, accessible policies

    Employees and managers should be able to understand the organisation’s expectations. Keep core policies organised, use plain language and make sure staff know where to find the current versions. Review documents when working practices or business needs change.

    Make roles and responsibilities clear

    Up-to-date role descriptions help people understand the purpose of their work, key responsibilities and reporting lines. They also give managers a more consistent basis for recruitment, onboarding, performance conversations and development planning.

    Keep employee records organised

    Define which records the organisation needs, who is responsible for maintaining them, and who is authorised to access them. Use appropriate access controls and handle personal information carefully. Retention and handling practices should reflect applicable requirements and the organisation’s policies.

    Build repeatable people processes

    Document the main steps for recruitment, onboarding, leave requests, performance reviews, training and employee departures. A simple checklist and clear process owner can help reduce missed steps and make the experience more consistent for employees and managers.

    Review the foundation as you grow

    HR documentation should be useful, not simply stored away. Schedule periodic reviews, gather feedback from managers and employees, and update processes when the organisation changes. Where specialist legal or regulatory advice is needed, seek advice appropriate to your circumstances.

    A practical next step

    Begin by identifying the three people processes that create the most confusion or repeated questions in your organisation. Assign an owner to each, document the current steps, and prioritise the changes that will make the biggest difference to clarity and consistency.

    This article provides general operational guidance and is not a substitute for legal, regulatory or employment advice tailored to your organisation.
